prompt:
The attached source+current-view contact depicts two separate Dungeon After Dark pixel-art objects. Generate ONE transparent-background atlas exactly SIX equal columns x TWO equal rows. Columns left-to-right: FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Row 1 race-circuits-race-descent-checkpoint; row 2 safe-services-restaurant-dining-booth. Each cell has one complete object, centered, consistent scale within its own row, safe transparent gutters, no text or labels, no clipping, no adjacent-cell bleed. Use true axis-aligned orthographic projection, never isometric/perspective. Preserve canonical source identity/materials/counts. We will only use the specified affected directions; the other generated cells are contextual.

ROW 1 — race descent checkpoint: source is a descending stair flight inside a hazard-marked doorway, not a single flat gate. Preserve its black/yellow hazard lintel, two upright side posts, red indicators, gray feet and stair flight. FRONT can be matched to the shown accepted FRONT. TOP must be overhead flight footprint: stair treads run along the descent axis, rails/posts at both sides, two square post caps and only a thin lintel edge; no full upright portal facade in XY. RIGHT and LEFT must show actual side elevation of the descending stair run under/behind the hazard posts, with coherent low-to-high step/riser profile, not just a vertical post. BOTTOM must show the full XY underside/support footprint of the stair structure with closed gray/black support/backing, not a thin doorway crossbar. REAR is the opaque back/structure of the checkpoint with the stair backs/steps and supports seen from the opposite end; do not repeat the front tread face or simple portal facade.
ROW 2 — safe-services restaurant booth: preserve exactly two red upholstered booth seats opposed on the X sides of a small beige table, with black bases and central black pedestal. FRONT and TOP may remain as shown. RIGHT and LEFT are camera views from the two X ends: broad outer red upholstered booth backs/ends occupy and occlude most of the table; table/pedestal is partially visible in the center, do not show a lone side chair profile. These opposite sides should reflect the fixed arrangement. BOTTOM is a true below-Z view of the full XY assembly: underside footprints of two distinct seat blocks on opposite X sides, centered table underside and central pedestal/base; no upright chair backs. REAR viewed from -Y shows the same two separate opposed seat backs/blocks around the table, not one continuous red bench or a single wide sofa.

Pixel-art outlines, textures, and palette must match the references. Hidden surfaces are conservative inferred illustrations, not recovered pixels.
